chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
When a man from a group gives the greeting of peace, it suffices on their behalf.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَ: It sufficed, was sufficient; a jurisprudential term indicating that an obligation has been discharged
key_terms.الْجَمَاعَة: The group or congregation; here referring to a group of people collectively
key_terms.سَلَّمَ: Gave the greeting of peace (al-salam alaykum); the act of offering the Islamic salutation

ai.seo_question: If one person in a group gives the Islamic greeting, does it count for the whole group?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes a legal ruling regarding the communal obligation of giving the Islamic greeting (salam). The Imam's statement through this chain indicates that the greeting of salam, while recommended for each individual, operates as a collective obligation (fard kifaya) in a group context — if one person fulfills it, the requirement is lifted from all others. This ruling reflects the Islamic principle that certain communal duties are discharged when any member of the group performs them.
